elements.name: Traceability
elements.documentation: The ability to track a product’s journey from origin to end-user – is crucial for non-profit and Public Health work. Whether distributing medicines, food aid, or other essential goods, organizations need end-to-end visibility to ensure products are authentic, safely handled, and actually reach intended beneficiaries. By assigning unique identifiers to products and capturing their movements in a digital system, stakeholders can quickly pinpoint where an item is at any given time or isolate issues (like a bad batch of medication) and initiate targeted recalls[1]. In low-resource settings, improving traceability boosts trust and reduces fraud, theft, and counterfeiting – common problems that undermine humanitarian efforts[2][3]. Overall, robust traceability systems enhance transparency and accountability, which are core values in Public Health supply chains.

elements.name: Point-of-service application
elements.documentation: Person-centred point of service system (PCPOSS) are digital systems that facilitate the provision and delivery of health services to individuals (i.e. persons, clients, patients, health service users) at the point of service or point of care. This includes software capabilities and embedded health interoperability standards that enable health workers to access, record and update individuals' health information, and to screen, manage, treat, and/or communicate with individuals. PCPOSS encompass community-based information systems, decision support systems, electronic health record systems and personal health records. (PDF 9, 18)

views.name: SF Reporting in the DIIG Enterprise Architecture (DTH SFP Fig. 3)
views.documentation: Substandard and falsified (SF) medical product reporting within the DIIG Digital Health Enterprise Architecture Framework (Section 3.2, Fig. 3, PDF 33-34): placing the SF Reporting Application in the Point-of-Service layer (specializing Point-of-service application), the NMRA Case Management Back End and Pharmacovigilance System in the Business Domain Services layer (linked into dth-sc Regulatory Systems and Quality Systems), and DPI-H registries (Product Registry, DPI-H Health Workforce Registry, Facility registry), Terminology Service, Identity Management Service, DPI-F Security & Consent Module, Update Subscription/Notification, and Interoperability Component in the foundational and interoperability layers.
